system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
### Project Kestrel — Buyer-side review

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general Warranty cap. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft; none has been given. | **Reject and restore 25%.** The proposed fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** basket; only loss above the basket recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** aggregate basket; once exceeded, liability from the **first dollar**. | **Reject and replace with the playbook thresholds and tipping basket.** Seller’s proposal materially suppresses otherwise valid claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; Seller also proposes limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24 months** for general Warranty Claims, without extending that regime to separate claim categories. An 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval; none has been given. | **Reject and restore 24 months.** The shorter fallback is unauthorised and the “all Claims” formulation risks overriding separate protections. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate regime with a **100% purchase-price cap**, limitation period of **at least six years**, and no general de minimis, basket or buyer-knowledge bar. | **Reject and insert a standalone Fundamental/Title regime.** Core ownership and authority risk must not be diluted by the general limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**; no express fraud-related carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insist on an express, overriding carve-out.** This protection is mandatory and cannot be waived under the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no deemed disclosure through the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches. | **Delete the general disclosures and require warranty-specific fair disclosure.** Bulk disclosure improperly transfers diligence and interpretation risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier should use defined, named **Seller knowledge persons**, subject to reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject the clause as drafted.** It converts constructive or adviser knowledge into a broad warranty defence and undermines negotiated disclosure standards. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours only; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | A genuine Completion condition requiring **effective Bluefen consent and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Strengthen the condition and prohibit deemed satisfaction on delivery alone.** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue and is a material customer. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require repayment and release through the Completion funds flow.** An unsecured promise to deliver a discharge later leaves Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD **420,000** Completion bonuses are said to be Seller’s responsibility but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are not addressed. | Express Seller funding or a specific Completion line item covering the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Revise the funds flow and allocate all associated costs expressly to Seller.** Silence risks the Company—and therefore Buyer—bearing a Completion-triggered liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; Seller regards it as adequate. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but neither non-payment nor payment is independently verified. | A broader indemnity covering losses arising from failure to obtain or perfect ownership/transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving Seller’s ability to cure by making the required payment and obtaining confirmation of transfer. | **Broaden the indemnity and require payment/assignment evidence.** The risk is defective IP ownership, not merely the amount of a disputed or unverified invoice. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure does not establish access, exact scope, notification duty, breach, loss or liability. | Preservation of logs and evidence, prompt investigation, regular Buyer updates, access to findings, and compliance/remediation obligations, without assuming a confirmed breach, notification duty, harm or monetary demand. | **Add investigation, preservation and reporting covenants while remaining fact-neutral.** The uncertainty must be managed without prematurely conceding either liability or immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD **330,000 aggregate**—are described as ordinary-course operating costs. | Further diligence on timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability; no automatic treatment as Debt or automatic purchase-price deduction. | **Reserve position pending assessment.** The current disclosure does not establish either ordinary-course treatment or a basis for a price adjustment. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller proposes that general limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated and treats Tax/IP as settled under that regime. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with clear priority language preventing hidden application of the general regime. | **Reject the universal limitations formulation and map each claim category expressly.** Otherwise general caps and time bars may inadvertently override negotiated category-specific remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 internal Company share register as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, valid issue, encumbrance-free title, authority and capacity, alongside updated registers and Completion transfer documents. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive proof; require independent verification.** A supplied internal register identifies the asserted source but does not independently establish good title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms expressly **open** for negotiation, with no assumption of unlimited liability or any agreed cap, period or allocation until resolved. | **Reject any statement that these terms are settled and reserve all rights.** No agreement has been reached, and they must not be absorbed silently into the general regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
